summary: Substrate is structurally sound + isolation invariants hold + documentation is largely honest with explicit wave-state limits. Three doc-vs-code drift MINORs (phantom test-family claims in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 5 verification-mechanism bullets, and an undocumented edge-body confidentiality scope in SECURITY-POSTURE.md). Two observations recorded around (a) production consumption gap (substrate wired but no production caller consumes scoped/namespaced writes yet at HEAD — expected v1-substrate posture per #1305 + #1301 named destinations) and (b) `pub` `derive_test_seam_key_from_cid_with_namespace` being called from production AEAD seal/unseal paths despite the `_test_seam_` name (Ben-ratified resolution at PR #1336 mr1 — rename skipped to avoid 5-callsite cascade; `_test_seam_` name itself is the load-bearing per-callsite signal). No BLOCKER. No MAJOR. Cross-check with L11 wire-format + L2 adversarial recommended for the two-CID + AEAD storage-layer surfaces.

findings.title: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 5 Verification mechanism bullet 3 cites a no-regression test that does not exist
findings.evidence: Bullet reads: 'A new no-regression test that scans `WriteContext` builder code paths for accidental `namespace_did = None` overrides post-write.' No file under `crates/benten-graph/tests/` implements this contract. The other two bullets (cargo-public-api baseline + tf1_989_cross_did_partition_isolation.rs) are real; only bullet 3 is phantom.
findings.fix_recommendation: Two valid HARD-RULE-12 options. (a) FIX-NOW path-(a): land the actual test as a tiny `tests/tf1_writectx_builder_namespace_did_no_clobber.rs` (the builder is `with_namespace_did(self, Option<Cid>) -> Self`; the test asserts that after `let ctx = WriteContext::new(l).with_namespace_did(Some(did)).with_authority(...)`, `ctx.namespace_did() == Some(&did)` — i.e. with_authority + future builder methods don't clobber the namespace field). One file, <40 LOC. (b) BELONGS-NAMED-NOW path-(b): re-word bullet 3 in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md to name a Composing-phase destination + remove the phantom claim; record a tracked row in docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-BUILD-BACKLOG.md (or phase-4-backlog.md) for the test to land. PIM-18 §3.6f / pim-1 §3.5b: doc-coupling sweep at G-CORE-9 freeze surfaces this bullet shape; recommend FIX-NOW path-(a) since the test cost is trivial.

findings.title: Edge-body confidentiality scope not documented (edges remain plaintext under namespaced writes; C2 AEAD applies to Node bodies only)
findings.location: docs/SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2297-2363 (Per-Node AEAD wrap layer + Inv-11 strengthening sections); crates/benten-graph/src/redb_backend.rs:1170-1192 (put_edge_with_context namespaced arm)
findings.evidence: `put_edge_with_context` namespaced path writes plaintext edge body + indexes under `d:<did>:e:<cid>` / `d:<did>:es:<src><edge>` / `d:<did>:et:<tgt><edge>` (lines 1184-1190). No AEAD wrap, no two-CID mapping. Confirmed: `grep 'AEAD\|encrypt' redb_backend.rs:1170-1200` returns no matches in the namespaced edge arm. The G-CORE-3d AEAD-wrap layer at lines 1666-1697 is keyed on `if let Some(did) = ctx.namespace_did.as_ref()` BUT only inside `put_node_with_context` — `put_edge_with_context` has no equivalent. SECURITY-POSTURE.md §'Per-Node AEAD wrap layer' (line 2297-) describes the C2 confidentiality contract in terms that a reader could plausibly interpret as 'everything under Some(did) is AEAD-wrapped' — the 'Inv-11 strengthening' subsection at 2339-2363 names 'C2 (confidentiality isolation, G-CORE-3d): per-Node AEAD with K(N) derived from K_principal' without scope-qualifying that edges fall under C1 partition isolation only.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add a one-sentence scope clarification in SECURITY-POSTURE.md §'Per-Node AEAD wrap layer' (right after the 'three load-bearing AEAD-layer defenses' bullet block at line 2310-2338) naming the edge scope explicitly: 'Scope: per-Node AEAD wrap applies to *Node body bytes* only. Edge bodies under a namespaced write remain plaintext under partition isolation (C1) — the per-DID partition keyspace (`d:<did>:e:<cid>`) is the only confidentiality layer for edges at this wave; cross-DID edge reads structurally miss at the key-prefix layer the same way Node reads do, but a same-DID attacker with raw redb access can inspect edge topology. Edge-body AEAD is named for a future wave if/when graph-topology confidentiality enters scope.' Tracked-row optional (BELONGS-NAMED-NOW): a `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md` line for 'edge-body AEAD wrap (post-v1-beta if untrusted-host topology confidentiality enters scope)'. Cross-check with L2 (adversarial threat model).

findings.title: Multi-tenant substrate is wired structurally but consumed by ZERO production engine call sites at HEAD (expected v1-substrate posture; documented; named)
findings.location: Workspace-wide: `grep -rn 'with_namespace_did' crates/benten-engine/src crates/benten-platform-foundation/src crates/benten-sync/src crates/benten-caps/src bindings/ packages/` returns no matches. Engine production sites: handler_versions.rs:204, engine_modules.rs:261/327, engine_views.rs:978, engine_caps.rs:685, manifest_signing.rs:608 all use `WriteContext::privileged_for_engine_api()` which carries `namespace_did = None`.
findings.evidence:
Audit results (HEAD = 4bbc4cac):
- `with_namespace_did(Some(_))` call sites: only in `crates/benten-graph/tests/tf1_989_cross_did_partition_isolation.rs` (tests) + `crates/benten-graph/tests/tf3d_partition_before_crypto.rs` (tests) + `crates/benten-graph/tests/tf3d_two_cid_mapping_roundtrip.rs` (tests) + `crates/benten-graph/src/browser_backend.rs:736` (single fail-closed test).
- `RedbBackend::scoped(did)` call sites in production engine: ZERO across benten-engine/benten-platform-foundation/benten-sync/benten-caps.
- `transaction()` post-commit fan-out is explicitly un-namespaced today + has a HARD-RULE-12-(b) named-destination at `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.7` (issue #1305) for transaction-path namespaced writes.
- The `ScopedView::get_by_property` surface is similarly named at §3.8 (issue #1306).
- napi/TS bindings expose ZERO partition surface (verified by `grep -rn 'namespace_did' bindings/ packages/`).
findings.fix_recommendation: Not a substantive finding against L5's lens. The lens question 1 ('every WriteContext construction site routes namespace_did through') reads as a production-coverage claim, but at the v1-beta substrate stage the structural seam exists + the consumer wire-up is HARD-RULE-12-(b) named to downstream waves (#1305 transaction-path, #1306 prop-index, #1301 encryption substrate wire-up). The multi-tenant *substrate* claim (per the L5 question 4 'Capability-gating ≠ confidentiality under untrusted-host; the seam exists for the encryption substrate to plug in; multi-tenant claim accurate?') IS accurate: the seam exists, partition isolation is structurally enforced (C1) + AEAD wrap is real (C2), AND the v1-beta production consumer wire-up is explicitly named for Phase-4-Meta-Composing (per CLAUDE.md baked-in #18 + #15 v1-gate scope). Recommendation: record this OBS in R6-R1-TRIAGE.md as 'positive observation' — the substrate-vs-consumer split is the *intended* v1-beta posture; surfacing the gap clearly is what R6's spec-to-code-compliance audit (pim-13 §3.12) is for. Cross-check with L8 (IVM + CanonicalViews seam) which has the parallel substrate-vs-consumer gap for IVM dispatch. NO ACTION at L5; the consumer wire-up is the next-phase scope.

findings.title: Production AEAD seal/unseal paths call a `pub`-exposed function named `derive_test_seam_key_from_cid_with_namespace`
findings.location: crates/benten-graph/src/redb_backend.rs:160 (pub fn); :1675 (production seal path call); :2678 (production unseal path call); docs/public-api/benten-graph.txt:851 (cargo-public-api baseline includes this `pub` fn)
findings.evidence: The K(N) source for both the seal-time `put_node_with_context` namespaced arm (line 1675) AND the unseal-time `read_decrypt_inner` (line 2678) is `derive_test_seam_key_from_cid_with_namespace(Some(did), &cid)`. The function is `pub` (not `pub(crate)`) — confirmed by cargo-public-api baseline at line 851. The `_test_seam_` hint in the function name is correct per the wave-state confidentiality limit documented at SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2406-2423 + the function's own doc-comment at lines 149-159, but the *naming* of a production-called function with `test_seam_` is a documented anomaly the function's doc-comment flags explicitly ('The `_test_seam_` hint in the function name is load-bearing on every caller until the K_principal-store backend lands; do NOT rely on the wave-3e confidentiality envelope for any data not also protected by namespace-isolation at the storage backend'). The rename to a non-test-seam name was explicitly considered + DEFERRED at PR #1336 mr1 fix-up: 'rename skipped to avoid 5-callsite cascade; the _test_seam_ name itself remains the load-bearing per-callsite signal'. Ben-ratified disposition; tracked at `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10` (K_principal-per-DID secret-material backend; line 171 explicitly names this swap-in).
findings.fix_recommendation: Not a substantive finding. The Ben-ratified resolution at PR #1336 mr1 fix-up explicitly chose to keep the `_test_seam_` name as the load-bearing per-callsite signal until the K_principal-store backend swap-in (named at §3.10). The function is `pub` because `tf3d_*` integration tests live in `crates/benten-graph/tests/` (not `src/`) and the test-seam pattern requires `pub`-reachable derivation for both seal/unseal sides + test corpus. Rename to `derive_k_principal_seam_key_from_cid_with_namespace` (drops `test_` connotation but keeps `seam` load-bearing signal) is a candidate Composing-phase fix-up coupled to the K_principal-store swap-in. Recommendation: record this OBS in R6-R1-TRIAGE.md as 'positive observation — the naming honesty is preserved at the function doc-comment + at SECURITY-POSTURE.md confidentiality-limit callout + at the named-destination row in phase-4-backlog.md §3.10; the rename is coupled to the substantive K_principal-source swap-in, not deferrable in isolation.' Cross-check with L1 (crypto-correctness) verifying the `_test_seam_` derivation path matches the spec; cross-check with L18 (pre-v1-freeze hygiene) verifying the public-API exposure of the test-seam name is ledger'd as a known pre-v1 limitation. NO ACTION at L5; consumer-side naming honesty is intact via the doc-coupling layer.

positive_observations: WriteContext shape per V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 5 is CORRECT at HEAD: `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute is applied; 4 fields (label, is_privileged, authority, namespace_did) all `pub`; `Default` impl carries `namespace_did = None`; builder + accessor names match the doc claim; cargo-public-api baseline matches.

Cross-DID partition isolation (C1) is structurally enforced at the key-prefix layer per `crates/benten-graph/src/store.rs:107-115`: `PARTITION_PREFIX = b"d:"` (sorts before all legacy single-letter prefixes `e`/`n`/`s` per byte ordering; verified comment-true). Every namespaced storage key family (`d:<did>:n:`/`e:`/`es:`/`et:`/`l:`/`c:`/`m:`) is structurally disjoint from un-namespaced (`n:`/`e:`/`es:`/`et:`). The C1 non-leak invariant is enforceable by inspection of `partition_prefix` builders + cannot be bypassed by generic-trait dispatch.

AEAD-binds-plaintext-CID rebinding-attack defense (Spike G/H + R3 ratification) IS LIVE: `crates/benten-graph/src/aead_wrap.rs:115-130` wraps with `aad_whole_content(plaintext_cid)` / `aad_per_chunk(plaintext_cid, chunk_index)`; tf3d_aad_binds_plaintext_cid_rebinding_attack.rs PIN 1 asserts substantive defeat (would-FAIL-if-AAD-omits-CID per pim-18 §3.6f).

Production seal/unseal paths route through the SAME `derive_test_seam_key_from_cid_with_namespace(namespace_did, plaintext_cid)` boundary: seal at line 1675, unseal at line 2678. Byte-for-byte agreement is load-bearing; AEAD authenticate-on-decrypt fails closed if K diverges; the structural-KDF chain (BLAKE3-keyed-hash K_principal → derive_root via HKDF-SHA256 → K(root) = K(N) at single-Node walk) matches Spike-E Interpretation-B + SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2374-2382.

Two-CID mapping table integrity (PIN 4 / tf3d_mapping_table_tamper_yields_typed_integrity_error) is enforced via `encrypted.plaintext_cid() != plaintext_cid` check at `read_decrypt_inner:2667-2672` BEFORE AEAD decrypt — tampered `plaintext_a → ciphertext_b` redirection caught by `TwoCidMapError::IntegrityMismatch`.

Non-redb backends fail-CLOSED on `Some(namespace_did)`: BrowserBackend at line 576-580 returns `GraphError::NamespacedWriteUnsupported`; SnapshotBlobBackend returns `ReadOnly` (different shape but equivalent failure intent — the read-only contract pre-empts the namespaced-write question). `GraphError::NamespacedWriteUnsupported` is `#[non_exhaustive]` per Fwd-2 #1207 with `backend: &'static str` payload; mapped to `E_NAMESPACED_WRITE_UNSUPPORTED` per crates/benten-errors/src/lib.rs:1672. Solid C1 substrate posture across all GraphBackend impls.

Confidentiality-limit-at-this-wave callout (mr1 MAJOR closure at PR #1336) is correctly placed at SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2406-2423 — explicit, honest, names the publicly-known-K_principal-from-namespace_did limit, names the production swap-in named destination (`docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10`).

CLAUDE.md baked-in #18 framing (Principal primitive: authority half vs confidentiality half) is correctly reflected at SECURITY-POSTURE.md:1872-1888 — the storage-partition substrate doc explicitly identifies '*authority* half of the multi-tenant isolation primitive' + names #1301 as the '*confidentiality* half' that this seam unblocks. No 'capability-gating = multi-tenancy' overreach found in spec docs (CLAUDE.md #18 concern about the prior ENGINE-SPEC.md:312 framing is moot — that line no longer exists in the current docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md).

Transaction-path namespaced-writes gap (#1305 / §3.7) + ScopedView::get_by_property gap (#1306 / §3.8) are correctly named per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b) with both inline source comments AND tracked GitHub issues AND named backlog rows. The C1 invariant is preserved at HEAD by `snapshot_subscribers_for(None)` filtering in the transaction() path — the gap is 'not expressible inside a transaction closure', not 'leaks'.
